speakers: Cem Karsan (guest, options and volatility strategist)
summary:
Karsan argues positioning and flows dominate markets and that the US is moving toward state-directed capitalism: backstopping Treasuries and a sovereign wealth fund buying equities by printing money, with a Warsh/Bessent good cop-bad cop split.
He maps a three-legged stool (flows, macro, administration) onto the calendar: calm to September, volatile to the midterms, weaker post-midterm until a mid-2027 push; plus the 'summer of George' vol-compression and dispersion regime. Opening segment covers June 2026 CTA performance and vol-manager frustration.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: around that time where where a lot of empires start to um to have you know not always right but question marks
claims.claim: Around the 250-year mark empires tend to face a critical juncture, layered on top of the shorter fourth-turning cycle, and the US is at one now.
claims.testable: no - single historical analogy, no defined signal

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: talking about how it was inevitable that oil would go to $200 or $150 or $200
claims.claim: Consensus experts in April-May 2026 called oil at $150-200 as inevitable because of the Iran crisis, and were wrong.
claims.testable: partly - consensus forecasts could be tested against outcomes

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: markets are super quick to remove that risk factor and bring things down to more normal level
claims.claim: Markets remove a crisis risk premium as soon as there is a small clearing of the air, even when experts say the crisis outcome is inevitable.
claims.direction: risk premium compresses fast after de-escalation
claims.testable: partly - could test oil/risk premia after de-escalation headlines

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: Nothing, literally nothing, is more important than positioning itself.
claims.claim: Positioning is the only reliable driver of outcomes because the net effect of who is long or short outweighs news (Soros reflexivity).

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: if the world is long, the odds are are much higher, right, that it will go down. And if the world is short, the odds are much higher that it will go up.
claims.claim: Crowded long positioning raises odds of a decline and crowded short positioning raises odds of a rally (contrarian positioning signal).
claims.conditions: not a certainty, a tailwind or headwind to the outcome
claims.testable: yes - positioning extremes vs forward returns

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: markets go up 20% in two months like they just did. That's $50 trillion of collateral.
claims.claim: Because equity markets are now so large (a 20% move is about $50T of collateral), positioning flows outweigh the effect of small liquidity changes or geopolitical news.
claims.testable: partly - market size vs flow impact

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: everybody thought they were positioned for something that was obvious and inevitable. So, once again, the opposite happened.
claims.claim: When everyone positions for an obvious outcome (oil spike on a Middle East war), the opposite tends to happen.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: everybody seems to have thrown in the towel and uh we have oil shorts at record highs now very quickly
claims.claim: Oil shorts have reached record highs after capitulation, which Karsan frames as a potential contrarian setup for oil to start rising.
claims.testable: yes - COT extremes vs forward oil returns

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: capex is driving everything but it's capex um that's not a very laborheavy capex right
claims.claim: The economy is K-shaped: AI infrastructure capex drives growth but is not labor-heavy, so jobs numbers soften while the capex-linked market stays strong.
claims.direction: soft labor data alongside strong equities

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: Earnings growth is 100% coming from that capex build and and it's a reflexive loop.
claims.claim: Index earnings growth comes entirely from the AI capex build, a reflexive loop where the market itself, not the broad economy, drives outcomes.
claims.indicator: S&P earnings growth contribution from AI capex

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: earnings last quarter was from the increased value of anthropic
claims.claim: A large share of one mega-cap's reported earnings came from mark-ups of its AI-lab stake rather than customer demand, showing earnings are inflated by capital-market valuations (speaker misnames the stake).
claims.indicator: mark-to-market gains on AI stakes in earnings

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: pretty solid first half of the year for CTAs and trend followers
claims.claim: Trend followers had a solid H1 2026 despite June reversals in energies and metals (silver, gold, base metals); currencies were the only bright spot in June.
claims.direction: trend following positive H1, negative June
claims.conditions: reversals in energy and metals hurt

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the beta 50 was down 1.76% for the month of June still up 7.76 for the um 2026
claims.claim: Data point: Beta 50 -1.76% in June and +7.76% YTD; SG CTA -1.09% (+9.27% YTD); SG Trend -1.29% (+9% YTD); short-term traders -0.31% (about +5% YTD).
claims.indicator: Beta 50, SG CTA, SG Trend, SG Short Term Traders

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: World government bonds not having a good year, down 75 basis points in June, down 37 basis points um so far this year
claims.claim: Data point: MSCI World +10% YTD (-0.69% June), world government bonds -0.37% YTD (-0.75% June), S&P 500 +10.21% YTD (-1% June); equities up while bonds weak in 2026.
claims.indicator: MSCI World, world govt bonds, S&P 500

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: there was no real money to be made from a longfall trade
claims.claim: Long-vol hedges earned nothing in the Q1 2026 drawdown (about 9-10%) because the decline was slow and grinding, and the fast rebound then hurt them.
claims.direction: long vol payoff low in slow declines
claims.conditions: slow decline followed by fast V-recovery
claims.testable: yes - vol-strategy returns by drawdown speed

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: hedging and using long vvall uh is always frustrating
claims.claim: Systematic long-vol hedging is chronically frustrating because it pays only in sudden moves, and hedges have repeatedly failed (2022, April 2025, 2026).
claims.testable: yes - long-vol carry cost vs payoff

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: callvall is inordinately cheap
claims.claim: Call volatility is cheap relative to the larger, faster upside moves now occurring (e.g. 50% in two months in hyperscalers), so right-tail convexity pays, especially with dispersion.
claims.indicator: call skew / call implied vol vs realised upside
claims.testable: yes - call vol vs realised upside moves

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: it's the more convex outcome and that can be right tail and left tail
claims.claim: Volatility strategies are the distribution of all outcomes and the convex bet that can win from either tail; right-tail players did well in 2026.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: more willing to use markets, the dollar, technology, policy as instruments of power
claims.claim: The US is moving from neutral referee of global capitalism to a more interventionist state using markets, the dollar, technology and policy as instruments of power (a single regime shift).

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: socialism/communism with with American characteristics
claims.claim: The US is adopting state-directed capitalism (government stakes, picking winners), analogous to China's capitalism with Chinese characteristics, because great-power competition forces it.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: once America starts moving and start makes a decision move aggressively. That's when regimes at least the last 250 years begin to change aggressively
claims.claim: The US reacts late to crises but once it decides to act it moves aggressively, and that is when regimes change; accumulated pressures are now forcing action.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: Unsustainable debt, populism which we've talked about at uh at length.
claims.claim: First pressures forcing regime change are unsustainable debt and populism, both accelerating.
claims.testable: partly - debt/GDP measurable, populism is not

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: baby boomers are dying and over the next decade we're going to hit you know a even greater populist impulse
claims.claim: Populism is accelerating as baby boomers die (examples: billionaire tax, proposals for 50% state ownership of AI firms) and becomes accepted on both sides.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: structural inflation which is not going away and if anything um accelerating
claims.claim: Structural inflation persists and accelerates due to global conflict, protectionism, fiscal spending and populism.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: cannot we can no longer allow a twoarter decline of more than 20%
claims.claim: The equity market is too big to fail: a two-quarter decline above 20% would drain liquidity and growth too much, so policy will not tolerate it.
claims.testable: partly - frequency of >20% two-quarter declines under the thesis

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: an intractable conflict with China to decide who is going to make the rules of the next 40, 50, 100 years
claims.claim: The US-China fight over who holds the primary reserve currency and sets the rules is the fifth pressure pushing for state action.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: they are going to create a sovereign wealth fund that buys within the next decade 10 to 15 trillion dollars of equities and they're going to do it by printing money
claims.claim: The US will back-stop the Treasury market and fund a sovereign wealth fund buying $10-15T of equities via money creation, using the dollar's exorbitant privilege.
claims.direction: long US equities, short purchasing power

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: Japan owns 8 to 9% of the DK. It's already been done before.
claims.claim: Precedent: Japan's central bank owns 8-9% of its equity market and Norway runs a ~$3T sovereign wealth fund, so state equity ownership via money creation has been done.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: printing money cannot happen in England or Turkey or Zimbabwe because they don't have natural structural demand for the currency
claims.claim: Only a reserve-currency issuer can print money at scale without a currency collapse, so the US can do what weaker countries cannot.
claims.conditions: only for currencies with structural demand

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: This is the fifth stake they've taken in a company.
claims.claim: The US government is taking equity stakes in firms (Intel 10%, others, OpenAI 5% offered), and Karsan expects stakes to rise to 10-20% each and then broaden into trillions.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: I believe it's in the next year. I think it's before June of next year
claims.claim: A moment is coming (before June 2027) when the government buys massive stakes across a broad swath of businesses worth over a trillion dollars, trillions within a year or two.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: you are essentially instead of taxing the rich and giving it to the poor in a traditional way, you are taxing the rich by simply taking stakes in those equity businesses
claims.claim: A state-funded equity fund short-circuits the populism of a K-shaped economy by giving everyone ownership instead of taxing the rich directly.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: the only way you get rid of the debt is through monetizing it anyway
claims.claim: The plan supports equities, competes with China and short-circuits populism but drives massive inflation, which is intended because monetization is the only exit from the debt.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: that market goes up that drives more investment in US businesses which drives growth
claims.claim: Government equity buying lifts the market (Intel rose about 40% on the stake), raising investment and growth, with proceeds going to the Treasury to back-stop social programs.
claims.testable: yes - event study of government stake announcements

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: greatest risk is that China quite frankly doesn't want the US to do this
claims.claim: The plan is not fair globally and the main risk is China (and the rest of the world) pushing back.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: after the midterms and before June in a meaningful way
claims.claim: Large-scale government equity buying will start after the Nov 2026 midterms and before June 2027, aiming to get markets moving ahead of the 2028 election.
claims.direction: long equities from post-midterm to mid-2027

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: feature not a bug that they keep taking it down to take it up again
claims.claim: The administration deliberately lets markets fall and then reverses to rally them, so expect repeated drop-then-rally cycles.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: Iran and Venezuela and Panama and Philippines are all about. They are creating a moat.
claims.claim: US actions in Iran, Venezuela, Panama and the Philippines aim to build a moat around dollar-denominated trade (commodities priced in dollars) against Chinese yuan trade.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: there's this period November to June where again uh you should expect um full throttle re-engagement
claims.claim: The Iran deal holds only until the midterms; expect full re-engagement and renewed oil/commodity volatility from November to June.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: the US wants to control trade as much as it can and it wants to make sure most importantly that trade is continues to be done in dollars
claims.claim: The US will not accept Iranian or Chinese control or taxation of Hormuz traffic in other currencies, so conflict continues beyond the nuclear justification.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: The administration also needs to and will in my opinion move more to the center.
claims.claim: After the midterms the administration will move to the centre by linking markets to populism (Trump and Sanders converging), which unifies both sides behind the plan.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: we'll probably get a pretty ugly November to June
claims.claim: The risk is infighting over who gets what; a crisis is what unites people, hence a messy November to June.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: They have a implicit if not explicit wink wink nod nod keep going we got your back
claims.claim: AI hyperscalers borrow to fund huge capex because of an implicit government backstop (buying their stock, bailing them out), and not playing along risks punishment.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: capex is different this time because there's an implicit guarantee the US government's going to keep driving that cap.
claims.claim: The AI capex cycle differs from the dot-com bubble because the US government implicitly guarantees it to compete with China.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: we are definitely in a bubble without um the investment and the promises and the control of the most big bully dominant force in the world
claims.claim: Valuations are a bubble that only holds because of government support (Fed, Treasury); without it the outcome is bad, so the question is whether they retain control.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: there's less control now and that means more risk.
claims.claim: The US waited 10-20 years to act, so the plan has less control and more risk, with China likely to poke at it (gray swans).

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: this is the don't fight the Fed thing, but on steroids with the whole US system
claims.claim: With the whole US system (Treasury, Fed, government stakes) behind the market, do not bet against it in the short to medium term.
claims.testable: partly - 'don't fight the Fed' as a rule

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: will things mean revert? Um in a natural system, yes.
claims.claim: Mean reversion applies in a natural market, but a state-managed market is probably not natural, so valuation-based reversion is less reliable.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: You need someone at the head of the Fed that at least appears and can initially act as if they are independent
claims.claim: Warsh is the good cop appearing independent to protect dollar credibility while Bessent is the bad cop pushing printing and stock buying; Fed independence is shrinking.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: the Federal Reserve will hop on and begin to backs stop
claims.claim: Sequence: the Treasury buys back its own debt first, then in a crisis the Fed backstops the long end of the curve.
claims.direction: long-end yields capped in a crisis

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: they're also not doing what the Japanese central bank did, which is just buy stocks themselves
claims.claim: The plan routes equity purchases through a Treasury sovereign wealth fund funded by borrowing and printing, not direct central-bank stock buying, because it looks fairer.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: volumes drop in half yet compre structured products stay the same
claims.claim: Summer of George: in summer, volumes halve while structured-product hedging stays constant, compressing volatility further.
claims.testable: yes - seasonality of vol and volume

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: whatever they're long tends to go down and whatever uh people are short tends to go up and you get massive dispersion
claims.claim: In compressed summer markets, hedge funds' long positions fall and shorts rise, producing large dispersion.
claims.direction: short crowded longs, long crowded shorts

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: if you have all compression at the index level, that tends to mean if something goes up, something else has to go down.
claims.claim: Index vol compression forces the net to zero, so single-name moves are offsetting and correlations break down in summer.
claims.testable: yes - implied correlation index vs dispersion

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: in that process you should do the opposite
claims.claim: In the summer-of-George regime, do the opposite of recent winners (fade momentum/positioning), and expect it for roughly the next month.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: There's three majors. There's flows.
claims.claim: Framework: short/medium-term markets are driven by three legs: flows (structural, including summer, year-end, midterm), macro (rates, inflation, growth) and the administration itself.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: flex structural flows are very positive until let's say September
claims.claim: Flows are positive until about September while macro is slowly degrading, so expect choppy but no negative fireworks; markets can also support macro via a reflexive loop.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: populist periods, elections matter more than ever
claims.claim: Election outcomes matter more in populist periods and especially this midterm, since losing both houses would stop the plan, so the administration will do all it can to hold the Senate.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: a two-month period where the flows are less positive, but the administration is very intent to keep it going
claims.claim: September to early November is a more volatile window: flows fade, macro worsens, administration pushes to support markets; do not bet against the administration.
claims.conditions: poor polls would make it more dangerous

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: The flows will be essentially gone after mid December
claims.claim: After the midterms macro worsens and flows disappear after mid-December, and the administration may allow a controlled crisis to reset.
claims.conditions: assumes they win the Senate; losing it would be worse

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: have an administration that probably wants a bit of a crisis, a controlled crisis, but a crisis.
claims.claim: The administration may want a controlled crisis post-midterm to take markets down and then rally them (take it down to take it up).

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: I would wait till the midterms then I would attack Iran
claims.claim: Karsan reads Trump's likely playbook as waiting until after the midterms and then attacking Iran, with inflationary effects.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: midterm years like which is this year right are historically the worst
claims.claim: Midterm years are historically the weakest for US equities, particularly Q2 and Q3.
claims.indicator: US equity returns in midterm years
claims.direction: equities weak in midterm years Q2-Q3

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: administration doing everything it can to stable the stabilize the ship in the short term because of the midterm
claims.claim: The oil spike did not materialize partly because of positioning and partly because the administration stabilised macro ahead of the midterm; now the oil-up bet is turning more interesting.
claims.direction: long oil as positioning has reversed
